standard_prerequisites.name: Uniformly continuous bounded functions, Gelfand algebras, ambits and orbit closures
standard_prerequisites.statement: For a topological group the right-uniformly continuous bounded functions form a C-star algebra on which the group acts by left translation, and for a function in that algebra the closed unital left-invariant subalgebra it generates has a Gelfand spectrum, a compact space on which the group acts with the identity character as a distinguished point; the pair consisting of this compact space and the point is the ambit of the identity. Dually, the closure of the orbit of the function under the action is a compact space with the function itself as distinguished point. The author's own definitions and the surrounding material of the article are the ones used by the counted statement and proof.
standard_prerequisites.use: The counted proposition identifies the two descriptions of the universal ambit attached to a function, and the article uses it to transfer statements about the Gelfand compactification to statements about orbit closures, which is the route its fixed-point results take.

core_obligations: Describe the function on the spectrum: the article's earlier section shows that a uniformly continuous bounded function may be viewed as the continuous function on the spectrum of the algebra it generates, given by evaluation at the point of the spectrum; this is what makes the comparison possible (source lines 434-436).

Define the comparison map: for a point of the spectrum, the map sending a group element to the evaluation of the function at the translated point is again a uniformly continuous bounded function, and this assignment defines a map from the spectrum into the orbit closure; the proof verifies that it is well defined, continuous and equivariant (source lines 436-444).

Show it is injective and surjective: two points of the spectrum that induce the same function on the orbit agree on the algebra generated by the function, hence coincide, which gives injectivity; surjectivity follows because the translates of the function are exactly the images of the translates of the distinguished point, and the orbit closure is the closure of that set (source lines 444-448).

Read off the isomorphism of ambits: the comparison map carries the distinguished point of the spectrum to the function itself and commutes with the action, so it is an isomorphism of ambits, which is the assertion (source lines 448-448).

proof_roadmap.step: View the function as an evaluation function on the spectrum of the algebra it generates.
Define the comparison map from the spectrum into the orbit closure and check it is continuous and equivariant.
Prove the comparison map is bijective by agreement on the generated algebra and by density of the orbit.
Conclude that the two ambits are isomorphic.

difficulty_reason: 计数单元是 doi:10.5802/ahl.16 的 Proposition prop:Gelfand（源 421-423 行，证明 434-448 行，15 行）：设 G 是拓扑群、f∈RUCB(G)，⟨f⟩ 为由 f 生成的单位左不变闭 C*-子代数，则 ambits (G^{⟨f⟩},e_G) 与 (cl(G·f),f) 同构。关键操作不是例行核验：证明要把 f 认成其 Gelfand 谱上的求值函数（434-436 行），再对谱中每个点构造从 G 到 orbit 的函数以定义比较映射并验证连续性与等变性（436-444 行），随后证明该映射**单**（两点若在 ⟨f⟩ 上一致则相等）与**满**（平移的像在 orbit 中稠密）从而得双射（444-448 行），最后核对它把 e_G 送到 f 因而给出 ambits 的同构（448 行）。难点在于把「代数侧的谱」与「函数侧的轨道闭包」之间的对应同时做到连续、等变且双射；原文位置在证明的 434-436、436-444、444-448、448 行。
